description: RA-02 defense in depth for in-process role assumption. When a process runs with SYSTEM_ROLE (surface_runtime launches every surface with SYSTEM_ROLE=<surface id>; `pnpm surfaces` and `pnpm config-mission` set it for their own runtimes), withExecutionContext / withExecutionContextAsync may only assume the SYSTEM_ROLE itself, the shared core roles (narrow libs/core store-writer roles), or the roles listed for that system role here; anything else throws [ROLE_ASSUMPTION_DENIED]. A SYSTEM_ROLE without an entry may only assume itself. Processes without SYSTEM_ROLE are unaffected. Lists are backed by the call-level reachability report docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts, RN-02: call sites and role-forwarding wrappers walked from each entry point, including child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE) and by opt-in runtime traces (KYBERION_ROLE_ASSUMPTION_TRACE, RN-01). The same bounds apply to a delegated child role (DR-01: a child spawned with buildExecutionEnv(env, role) under an inherited SYSTEM_ROLE runs as role only when this policy lets SYSTEM_ROLE assume it; the report counts each such call as an assumption site). A grant is only removed when the report proves it unreachable and no trace observed it; scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.contract.test.ts fails when a reachable role is missing. See knowledge/product/governance/AUTHORITY_MODEL.md section 3.B2.

shared_core_roles.rationale: Narrow roles that libs/core modules assume internally on behalf of their callers to write their own governed stores: infrastructure_sentinel (work coordination, peer messaging, mesh, the stimuli journal), knowledge_steward (mission creation), scope_locale_reader (read-only: libs/core/locale.ts reads the tenant reply locale, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/locale.json, bound to the turn's tenant, for every surface that renders a reply), and the GovernedArtifactRole set of artifact-store / surface stores (chronos_gateway, slack_bridge, surface_runtime; surface-coordination-store maps a surface to its role from a governed plus a personal-tier map, so any GovernedArtifactRole is reachable wherever it is used). operational_learning_writer is deliberately restricted to the system roles that reach its learning path. The broad roles (ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge) are never shared: each system role lists them only where docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json reaches them. The report shows oauth_callback_surface and surface_runtime do not reach some shared roles; they stay shared because removing a shared role for one system role needs a policy-shape change (tracked as a follow-up). chronos_tenant_runner and organization_operator are reached through the agent-runtime supervisor daemon child process (resident-dot sweep): chronos_tenant_runner lists and reads knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/dots/ charters bound to that tenant (same rule as chronos tenant pipelines), and organization_operator runs scheduled organization operation pipelines bound to the operation's tenant/organization (DL-06). Both are assumed internally by libs/core / the governed operation executor on behalf of whichever surface started the daemon, never by the surface itself.

chronos_mirror_v2.rationale: Chronos viewer-scoped routes assume chronos_localadmin / chronos_operator (withViewerExecutionContext*, plugin-host-boot tenant registry reads); chronos_token_registry_reader: lib/viewer-context.ts and lib/api-guard.ts read the chronos-access viewer token registry (its only grant), plus libs/core authn-providers (registry-token provider); generation_scheduler: the schedule quick action runs libs/core generation-scheduler in-process. reconcile_config_fallbacks (added by RN-03): the same quick action loads the media-generation actuator in-process, whose capture action runs system-actuator pipeline ops including reconcile-ops (libs/core/reconcile-ops.ts); Chronos can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope (knowledge/, public and confidential tiers) covers the grant's allow_write paths, so this adds no effective authority. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable. RN-01: the plugin-views E2E (surface-runtime mode) and the Chronos vitest suite under SYSTEM_ROLE=chronos_mirror_v2 observed chronos_gateway, chronos_localadmin, chronos_operator, chronos_token_registry_reader and mission_controller, all listed.

The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable. chronos_token_registry_reader is deliberately absent: computer-surface/auth.ts passes `registrations: null` (TR-01), recorded as reviewed-infeasible in the report.

concierge.rationale: Concierge routes assume sovereign_concierge directly (config-missions, ingest, me, members, memory-queue, notification-preferences, plugins, setup, training, work-inventory) plus libs/core authn-providers, browser-onboarding, slack-onboarding, tool-runtime-policy; withConciergeViewerContext assumes concierge_localadmin / concierge_operator; chronos_token_registry_reader: lib/viewer-context.ts and libs/core authn-providers read the chronos-access viewer token registry. ingest_commit (added by RN-03): /api/ingest runs scripts/ingest.ts as a child with buildExecutionEnv(process.env, ...), which keeps SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge, and the ceremony commits as ingest_commit (libs/actuators/ingest-actuator/src/commit.ts); Concierge can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope (knowledge/, public and confidential tiers) covers the grant's allow_write paths, so this adds no effective authority. Since DR-01 the child runs as the delegated role sovereign_concierge (KYBERION_DELEGATED_ROLE, AUTHORITY_MODEL.md 3.B2) but keeps SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge, so its in-process ingest_commit assumption is still bounded by this entry and the grant stays. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller: reachable per docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable.

nexus_daemon.rationale: presence/bridge/nexus-daemon.ts dispatches reflexes to the service actuator in-process, whose service reconciliation starts `node dist/libs/actuators/<id>/src/index.js` for any manifest id with process.env (SYSTEM_ROLE inherited), and dispatchFeedback runs the channel-registry connector actuator the same way: every actuator entry point is reachable. ingest_commit (ingest-actuator commit) and reconcile_config_fallbacks (system-actuator reconcile op) are therefore added by RN-03; nexus_daemon can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope (knowledge/, public and confidential tiers) covers both grants' allow_write paths, so they add no effective authority. The actuator children are started with process.env and no explicit role, so they run as nexus_daemon (DR-01 delegation only applies to an explicit buildExecutionEnv role) and the grants stay. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). oauth_callback_surface.rationale: scripts/oauth_callback_surface.ts. sovereign_concierge: completeOAuthCallback resolves tool binaries through libs/core tool-runtime-policy (getToolRuntimePolicy). RN-03 removed ecosystem_architect and mission_controller: docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json proves neither reachable (no unresolved sites, no child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE) and RN-01 traces (hermetic smoke of the built surface, oauth_callback_surface vitest suites under SYSTEM_ROLE) only observed surface_runtime (the surface's own callback write, a shared core role).

operator_surface.rationale: Read-only audit monitor (presence/displays/operator-surface), operator-launched through surface_runtime with SYSTEM_ROLE=operator_surface. sovereign_concierge and chronos_token_registry_reader: reachable per docs/developer/role-assumption-reachability.json via libs/core surface-authn -> authn-providers (module providers and loadRegistrations). mission_controller is reachable via data.ts#getCloudflareOsSnapshot -> CloudflareOsSurface -> CloudflareOsControlPlane -> decideApprovalRequest (held_effect settlement is always filed under mission_controller). ecosystem_architect is reachable via a spawned orchestration worker's deployment-adapter config load. The surface also has unresolved sites (provider-discovery memoized CLI spawn, a computed import in src/lib/view.ts), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable.
